question: In github.com/payloadcms/payload, `commitTransaction` appears as a database-adapter method, a utility wrapper, a type, and per-adapter implementations. Which single file and function provides the DEFAULT no-op `commitTransaction` (`() => Promise.resolve(null)`) that `createDatabaseAdapter` assigns so an adapter that does not implement transactions still has a callable method? Name the file.
critical_facts: names packages/payload/src/database/createDatabaseAdapter.ts as the file holding the default no-op commitTransaction

identifies it as the module-level `const commitTransaction: CommitTransaction = () => Promise.resolve(null)` (around line 22) that is placed into the returned adapter object as a default before `...args` can override it
material_errors: names the utility wrapper packages/payload/src/utilities/commitTransaction.ts (which calls payload.db.commitTransaction and deletes req.transactionID) as the no-op default
names a real adapter implementation (packages/db-mongodb/src/transactions/commitTransaction.ts or packages/drizzle/src/transactions/commitTransaction.ts) as the default
names the type declaration packages/payload/src/database/types.ts (`commitTransaction: CommitTransaction`) instead of the no-op default value
evidence: packages/payload/src/database/createDatabaseAdapter.ts:45 — `commitTransaction,` placed in the returned adapter defaults, then `...args` (line 57) spreads the adapter's own impl over it
burden: `git grep -n "commitTransaction" -- packages` = 84 match lines across 42 files
